generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table, never NULL; PK columns are excluded from group-size, NULL and freshness rewriting.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from the parent table's FINAL generated primary-key values (after all post-processing); allow NULL only if the column is nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.real_quantity: Positive real numbers drawn from a log-uniform distribution over [1, 1e8]; round to 1 decimal.
generic_sampling_rules.real_rate: Real numbers in [0, 1] rounded to 4 decimals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Random title-cased words, 1-3 words, length 3-40 characters.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Random person-like name: title-cased first and last word, length 5-40 characters.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Uniform choice from the column's enum list (see per_column_exceptions).
generic_sampling_rules.text_near_variant: For LIKE/equality literals, generate the literal itself plus near-variants (case change, one extra character, one substituted character) with 20% share.
generic_sampling_rules.text_date_range: Format 'Month D-D' or 'Month D' with a valid month name and day 1-28.
generic_sampling_rules.numeric_boundary: For each listed literal L, include L-1, L, L+1 (or step-scaled) with equal share; remaining values uniform in the column's range.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, at least one NULL row per instance and a NULL share following the compact database's share for that column (5-30% for the listed null_targets); the rest get non-NULL values; planted NULLs are never replaced to satisfy a rule.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_share: For DISTINCT-targeted columns, 20-50% of rows reuse an already-generated value.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_share: For ORDER/LIMIT-targeted columns, plant at least two rows sharing the boundary value.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: 70% of text values are fresh; 30% may repeat an earlier value.

targets.format: number with thousands separator + unit in parentheses, e.g. '1,370 lb (635 kg)'

dependencies.note: composite primary key; generate distinct pairs

semantic_rules_and_formulas.condition: International_Passengers IS NOT NULL AND Domestic_Passengers IS NOT NULL AND Transit_Passengers IS NOT NULL

semantic_rules_and_formulas.formula: Winning_Pilot IS NULL OR CAST(Winning_Pilot AS INTEGER) IN (SELECT Pilot_Id FROM pilot)
Winning_Aircraft IS NULL OR CAST(Winning_Aircraft AS INTEGER) IN (SELECT Aircraft_ID FROM aircraft)

pilot.Age range: min 20, max 37 in shown rows; widened to 18-70

uncertainty: match.Winning_Pilot and match.Winning_Aircraft are TEXT but reference integer PKs; generation stores the integer as text and fills them from the FINAL parent PK set after all post-processing.
airport_aircraft.ID is nullable and not a key; treated as a free integer.
airport_aircraft sample contains Airport_ID=9 which is not in the shown airport rows; generation restricts to generated parent keys.
match.Fastest_Qualifying is a free text name, not a FK; no formula stated.
airport.%_Change_2007 is text; no numeric range rule enforced beyond format.

Total_Passengers boundary values (9999999/10000000/10000001) are planted by back-solving one of International/Domestic/Transit so the sum rule still holds on those rows; rows with a NULL component keep the boundary value directly.
match.Winning_Pilot/Winning_Aircraft are excluded from group-size planting because they are FK copies of integer PKs; group-size targets are realized on aircraft.Aircraft and pilot.Age instead.
The 'duplicate_share' is interpreted as the share of rows that copy an earlier value (20-50%).
